sources.note: No prosodic features coded (no 13A tone, no 14A-17A stress/rhythm datapoints). StressTyp2 dump held by the project likewise has no Wuzlam entry (only the ISO code row).

sources.citation: Kinnaird, William (1997). Ouldeme tone sketch. Yaoundé: SIL. SIL Cameroon. 17 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The language is not in the catalog and there are no existing stress statements; this work adds nothing on stress. It does document a three-level tone system, which is relevant if the catalog wants a 'tonal, no stress statement' entry, but it is not a statement about stress.

sources.citation: Kinnaird, William J. & Anni M. Kinnaird. 1998. Ouldeme narrative discourse: outline of principal features. Yaoundé: SIL. 34 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Discourse study; no phonology; only tone mention is the mid-tone aorist prefix. Silent on stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. Utrecht: LOT (375).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: de Colombel, Véronique. 2006. Lieu, temps et déplacements dans la langue ouldémé. In S. Naïm (ed.), La rencontre du temps et de l'espace: approches linguistique et anthropologique, 121-137. Louvain: Peeters. (HAL hal-04612205)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress; notes three tone levels on the verbal mode vowel (mid = realis, high = potential, low = hypothetical).

sources.citation: de Colombel, Véronique. 2000. Comparaison des noms et usages de six cents plantes dans les groupes tchadiques des monts du Mandara (Cameroun): synchronie dynamique et diachronie, linguistique et ethnolinguistique. Vol. I. Thèse de Doctorat d'État, Univ. Paris V (dir. J.M.C. Thomas). 260 pp. scan on HAL tel-04124160 (reprints her 1986b BSL, 1987a La Linguistique, 1987d Hamito-Semitic Congress, 1982b and 1987b Ouldémé papers).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement on Ouldémé word accent in 260 pp. The phonology reprints treat phoneme combinatorics, syllable/tone schemes of monemes, tense (T+/T-) initial consonants conditioning H vs L tone on verb bases (52%/48%), vowel system and 'expansion vocalique'. 'accent' appears only generically (what a quantitative phonology should record: 'la position et la hauteur des accents et des tons'; critique of Chomsky & Halle).

sources.citation: Kinnaird, William & Oumaté Timothée (eds.), with Z. Mokfetya, G. Féfé and the Comité d'orthographe. [1999/2003]. Dictionnaire ouldémé–français. Yaoundé: SIL. 154 pp. (4,750 entries).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Front matter gives alphabet and tone-marking conventions only (tone of each headword given in parentheses with H/M/L diacritics); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kinnaird, William, Annukka Kinnaird & Oumaté Timothée (et le comité d'orthographe). 1999. Proposition d'orthographe pour la langue ouldémé. Yaoundé: SIL. 29 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. Sections 2.1-2.4, 3.2 cover consonants, vowels (incl. epenthetic schwa), and tone (three tones, 'le ton est, pour la plupart, entièrement prévisible' for native readers; tone written only where ambiguous). 'accent' occurs only in the sense of diacritic tone marks.

sources.citation: Kinnaird, William. 1997. Ouldeme tone sketch [running title: Outline of Ouldeme Tone]. Yaoundé: SIL / Ministère de la Recherche Scientifique et Technique. 17 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: the words stress/accent do not occur in the 17 pp. Describes a three-level tone system: '2.1 Tone patterns. In isolation or in the citation form, all lexical items carry a definite tone pattern in Ouldeme: either high, mid or low tone in one syllable words or a combination of those in longer words' (p.2); 8 of 9 two-syllable melodies attested (LM absent); depressor consonants (voiced non-implosive obstruents) block H-spreading; most verb roots analysed as toneless with default L; H- and L-tone spreading in the phrase. Reviews Provoost 1987 (sect.21, 107) and de Colombel 1986/1996 on…
